newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba official says EMU collapse bad for Germany.
newsitem.headline: Buba official says EMU collapse bad for Germany.

text.p: Germany would stand to suffer dire consequences if efforts to launch a common European currency collapsed, a senior Bundesbank official said on Monday.

"If the European currency union does not happen it would signal a step backwards in the process of European integration leading to a return of individual economic policies," Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher warned.

"Especially for Germany this would have devastating consequences," Kuehbacher, also president of the regional central bank of Berlin and Brandenburg, added in a speech prepared for delivery to a banking audience.
A copy of the text, which is virtually identical to one Kuehbacher delivered nearly two weeks ago, was made available beforehand.

In the run-up to Europe's currency union, scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999 with as many nations as meet the strict entry criteria, Bundesbank officials have stepped up efforts to inform the public about the currency union, giving speeches increasingly often.
